Messages.Author: Gregory Stuart Pettigrew
Messages.Body:
Malkavian Antitribu, Grou 4, Capacity 6
dem vic AUS OBF

Sabbat: Drusilla may give you control of a ready Ventrue for the
remainder of the turn as a (D) action that costs 2 blood.

Not sure how useful her special will be, Ventrue aren't known for
staying untapped to block. Still, she can play Soul Decoration.

--
- Gregory Stuart Pettigrew

Messages.Author: Merlin
Messages.Body:


You need it spelled out for you, eh?

I was thinking that she'd do ok in a Malk + For Force of Will/Torpor
machine, with OBF for responsible bleeding and copious stealth. Maybe
some of her new friends will have for/FOR (Apache Jones and White Lily
do, checking the spoilers), and there is Jason, the World's Voice and
J. Oswald Hyde-White as well.

It's of course ludicrous to suggest dropping "a bunch of Force of Will
in [my] Malkavian Antitribu deck, just in case Drusilla runs into
Ventrue," but if the deck is built to play the cards anyway it's not
such a waste, and it could be beneficial. Hell, the deck could play FOR
skills (For Drusilla as well as the Deranged), Heidelberg, Derange, and
Malakavian Dementia (Parthenon probably a must as well, with that
arrangement) and just do it *more* often if the Ventrue show up.

I played with a guy the other day who has "an answer to Arika" in every
single deck he plays, due to the Arika deck that his friend plays
frequently. He'll like Drusilla, i think.

Merlin

!Malks with Fortitude are useful, in a balls-to-the-wall fashion, but
!Malks with Vicissitude, while not as effective, are thematically
nicer, in "I can make you look like I feel" -way. And as most of my
games are casual ones, thematics matter (almost) as much as brutal
efficiency.

Personally I am just happy that the design team did not create another
Dolphin Black, or another multiacting stealth bleeder.

Right. It's not that Drusilla's special isn't cornercase; it is. Trying
to actually use it's going to require a serious amount of planning as
well as luck (to have a ventrue player on the right or left, not just

pretty low.
